label: Last original token / <DEL> of long (L=8-9) sequences starting with h, x, n, 0 or 1
explanation: Sparse feature that fires only at the end of the original phase of long sequences: on the <DEL> step (65% of mass) and the last original token (35%), almost always at t=8 or 9 with L=8 or 9 (86% of mass from L=9). It never fires in the copy phase or before t=7, and never for L<=6. Within this window, what the sequence starts with matters most: first token h gives 12x lift and about half the mass, and x, n, 0, 1 add more. The strongest activations are h-initial L=8/9 sequences, often with u/v/w late in the sequence. Precision is low (about 6% on dev). Most end-of-long-sequence steps, even ones starting with h, stay silent, and no simple token-history condition I tried (u/v/w seen, prev tokens) separates them. So the predicate gives the position and context where it can fire, not a full explanation.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=h (+5.86), orig0=n (+3.67), orig0=x (+3.43), prev_tok=v (+3.15), prev_tok=w (+3.09), orig0=0 (+2.99). Lower it: phase=2 (-6.53), next_out=- (-5.86), orig7=- (-4.94), orig8=- (-3.36).
